picks.title: Radiologists, LLMs fail at spotting AI-generated chest x-rays
picks.excerpt: Seoul National University Hospital tested radiologists and LLMs on 40 real and 120 synthetic chest x-rays; neither was reliable enough to be the primary safeguard, so the authors urge cryptographic credentials or watermarking to guard image authenticity.
picks.rationale: This is a reader study from Seoul National University Hospital: neither radiologists nor LLMs can reliably tell synthetic chest x-rays from real ones. That is a direct patient-safety and image-integrity problem for clinical imaging, and the authors call for provenance controls.

picks.title: OpenEvidence drew 271M queries from 952,000 clinicians in 2.5 years (JAMA study)
picks.excerpt: A JAMA cross-sectional study (doi 10.1001/jama.2026.21868, online 2026-10-15) characterizes clinician use of the AI clinical information platform OpenEvidence: 271M queries from about 952,000 clinicians, by clinician type, specialty and query purpose. Primary source is jamanetwork.com (Cloudflare-blocked).
picks.rationale: A new JAMA study is the first large-scale look at how clinicians actually use an AI point-of-care tool: 271M queries from about 952,000 clinicians. Becker's carries a fetchable body, whereas the JAMA page is blocked.

picks.title: AMA releases governance framework for agentic AI in healthcare
picks.excerpt: The American Medical Association released a governance framework for AI agents in healthcare, as industry groups issue guidance on agentic AI in the absence of federal regulation.
picks.rationale: This is a new official release from the largest US physician body: a governance framework that health systems can apply to AI agents in care. No federal rule covers this yet.

picks.title: An AI framework for end-to-end rare disease phenotyping from clinical notes using large language models
picks.excerpt: An LLM-based framework operationalizes the full rare disease phenotyping pipeline from clinical notes, replacing labor-intensive manual curation of structured phenotypes used in rare disease diagnosis.
picks.rationale: An LLM pipeline turns free-text clinical notes into the structured phenotypes used to diagnose rare diseases. It targets a real diagnostic bottleneck for patients, and the open-access body can be fetched.

picks.title: AI-based hourly prediction of emergency department demand integrating social determinants of health
picks.excerpt: An AI model forecasts hourly ED arrivals using social determinants of health alongside temporal and weather signals, aiming at proactive ED staffing against crowding linked to delayed treatment and mortality.
picks.rationale: This model forecasts emergency-department arrivals hour by hour so hospitals can staff ahead of crowding, which is linked to delayed treatment and deaths. It is a hospital-operations use case, and the open-access body can be fetched.

alternates.title: Are Med Students Cheating if They Use AI?
alternates.excerpt: At the AHCJ Fall Summit, Cedars-Sinai's Graciela Gonzalez-Hernandez argued AI use in medical school is not plagiarism and described an AI-friendly curriculum that teaches prompt construction.
alternates.rationale: Conference-talk reporting on AI in medical education. It is fresh, but it is a talk rather than a release or study, so it is the first alternate.

alternates.title: Announcing JAMA AI - A New Journal From the JAMA Network
alternates.excerpt: JAMA AI, the 14th JAMA Network journal, launches in early 2027 to publish clinical research on AI and computational tools applied to patient care.
alternates.rationale: A journal launch with no change to care, and the page is Cloudflare-blocked, so it is the second alternate.

dedup.note: The pool had 18 candidates, no clusters and 3 history_match tags. DROPPED as the same story: (1) Radiology Business 'adapting adult radiology AI models to pediatric population' (related, 0.22). It reports on a Nature Biomedical Engineering paper that adapts adult chest x-ray AI to children using multi-hospital data that never leaves each site. That is the same paper and event as the 10-14 card on s41551-026-01812-6 (adult radiograph models repurposed for neonatal care through continual learning, international multicentre), and the news write-up carries nothing new. Earliest wins. (2) STAT Clairity direct-to-patient (likely-repeat, 0.423). This is the same Clairity consumer-access launch published 10-08 via AuntMinnie/Everlywell. (3) STAT 'AI sandboxes' newsletter (related, 0.198). This is behind-the-scenes commentary on the state-regulation lobbying story published 10-15 and reports no new decision. DROPPED as commentary or opinion: AuntMinnie HPI rebuttal on the radiology workforce; Becker's UChicago CMIO interview; Endpoints clinical-reasoning panel; MedCity 'agentic AI stripped down' op-ed; NEJM AI medical-education perspective. DROPPED as stale or low priority: AuntMinnie JACR turnaround study (10-08, 8 days old, and thematically near the 10-08 private-practice efficiency card); npj sepsis ICU-stay model (10-09; kept the fresher npj items instead); JAMA Network Open public-perceptions survey (Cloudflare-blocked, survey only). Alternates are MedPage med-student AI and the JAMA AI journal launch. The AMA framework is a distinct official release by the AMA, not a follow-up to STAT's 10-15 lobbying story, which covered state-level advocacy. Diversity: nature.com 2, auntminnie 1, beckershospitalreview 1, healthcaredive 1, for 4 distinct outlets. No pick touches biosecurity or gain-of-function.
